themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 5 complaints last week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1900% spike (z-score: 10.97)—suggesting a possible cluster of lead exposure incidents in Fordham/University Heights that warrants immediate investigation into affected buildings and families.
evidence: 5 lead complaints filed last week vs. 0.2 average per week over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.97 indicates statistically significant anomaly (severity: high)
Lead exposure is health emergency for children and pregnant residents
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings generated lead complaints; interview residents about water testing and paint hazards
Contact NYC Department of Health to determine if complaints are clustered geographically or if a specific contamination source has been identified
Map lead complaints against older housing stock and recent renovation permits (242 alteration filings in past 90 days) to assess if construction work may have triggered lead dust exposure

themes_detail.label: SPIT enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints exploded to 5 this week compared to 0.1 per week baseline—a 3900% spike (z-score: 14.74, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)—indicating rapid escalation of code enforcement activity or newly discovered violations in the district.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 14.74 is the highest statistical anomaly in the entire dataset (severity: high)
SPIT is NYC's most aggressive enforcement unit, typically targeting chronic code violators
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development to determine what triggered SPIT activation this week and which properties/landlords are under investigation
Interview residents in affected buildings about conditions and timing of inspection notices
Cross-reference SPIT complaints against heat/hot water and plumbing complaints (which rank #1 and #5 overall) to assess if enforcement is response to systemic maintenance failures

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 19 two weeks ago versus 4.6 weekly average—a 311% spike (z-score: 3.62)—suggesting either a crackdown on street vendors in the district or a surge in illegal vending operations that residents are actively reporting.
evidence: 19 vendor enforcement complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 4.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.62 indicates statistically significant spike (severity: high)
Community board budget requests include 'Provide more sanitation trucks' suggesting ongoing vendor/street management tensions
reporting_angles: Determine if this reflects a coordinated enforcement action by NYPD or Department of Consumer Affairs, or organic rise in vendor activity
Interview street vendors and residents around commercial corridors (Fordham Rd, University Ave) about what changed in past 2 weeks
Assess whether vendor complaints correlate with foot traffic changes or seasonal economic factors in the district

themes_detail.label: Water conservation complaints rise
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints spiked to 5 last week versus 1.2 weekly average—a 300% increase (z-score: 3.13)—potentially indicating a new water main break, pressure issues, or conservation mandate affecting the district.
evidence: 5 water conservation complaints filed last week vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.13 indicates statistically significant anomaly (severity: high)
Complements overall water issues: 644 water leak complaints and 1071 plumbing complaints in 90-day period
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to confirm if water main break, pressure loss, or conservation order has been issued for Fordham/University Heights area
Interview residents about whether they've experienced low water pressure, discolored water, or conservation notices in past 2 weeks
Cross-reference with plumbing and water leak spikes to assess if infrastructure crisis is driving multiple complaint types

themes_detail.label: Obstruction complaints cluster
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped to 6 last week versus 1.9 weekly average—a 220% spike (z-score: 3.25)—suggesting emerging sidewalk, street, or building entrance blockages that may indicate illegal parking, construction debris, or vendor encroachment.
evidence: 6 obstruction complaints filed last week vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.25 indicates statistically significant spike (severity: high)
Illegal parking complaints remain high at 2243 over 90 days, suggesting broader sidewalk/street access issues
reporting_angles: Map obstruction complaints geographically to identify if they cluster on specific streets or near specific institutions (Fordham University, Bronx Community College)
Determine if obstruction spike correlates with recent construction permits (242 alteration filings) that may have generated debris or staging
Interview residents about what types of obstructions are causing problems and whether enforcement response has been adequate
